diet.text: Rodents, birds, frogs, lizards and other snakes

overview.text: The Speckled Kingsnake, or 'salt-and-pepper snake', is a non-venomous kingsnake of the central and southern United States. Like other kingsnakes it will eat other snakes.

identification.text: Black with a small yellow or white speck in the middle of almost every scale.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually up to about 1.2 m (48 in); the record is about 1.8 m (72 in).

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Central and southern USA, from southern Iowa south to the Gulf of Mexico (Missouri, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Oklahoma). In the west it blends with the Desert Kingsnake.

habitat.text: Prefers wetter places than other kingsnakes, such as swamps and rivers, but also uses woodland and grassy fields.

behaviour.text: When threatened it shakes its tail like a rattlesnake, releases a smelly musk and may bite. It usually calms down quickly and is often kept as a pet.

diet.text: Kills by squeezing (constriction). Eats birds, rodents and other mammals, frogs, lizards and other snakes.

recognise.text: Black body with a pale speck on nearly every scale.
